title: Benchmark priming checklist for multi-model fanout
content:
Purpose:
This note is a hands-on checklist and operational guide for priming and repeating throughput benchmarks in multi-model fanout scenarios. "Multi-model fanout" means one logical API route may route requests simultaneously to multiple compatible model variants (canary vs stable, quantized fallback, or ensemble members) and therefore exercises shared GPU/CPU/network resources in non-obvious ways. The goal: ensure runs are repeatable, avoid cross-variant cache interference, and produce defensible throughput/latency numbers for capacity planning and regression detection.

Scope:
- Applies to hosted and Dedicated environments where multiple model variants can co-reside on the same node pool or share network/NVLink interconnects.
- Focuses on warmup/priming, seed traffic, load generator config, and run hygiene for throughput runs (requests/s and tokens/s).

Quick summary (TL;DR):
1) Isolate the fanout topology to be tested (which variants, routes, fallback rules).
2) Run a multi-phase priming sequence: micro-primer, staggered-coldfill, steady ramp.
3) Capture full telemetry (per-variant p50/p95/p99, tokens/s, GPU occupancy, KV cache hit rate).
4) Repeat at least 3 independent runs with seeded RNG and compare run-level CV < 3% for primary metrics.

Definitions and failure modes unique to fanout:
- KV Cache Cross-Pollination: a heavy primer on one variant can populate shared caches (KV/prefix) that bias subsequent variant performance.
- Routing Amplification: small fanout misconfiguration creates disproportionate load on a single node (sticky routing or topology mismatch).
- Variant Starvation: when a quantized/fallback variant uses lower memory, it still competes for bandwidth or scheduling slots, causing oscillations.

Experiment naming convention (required):
bench/<route>-fanout/<variants>-seed<NN>-run<R>. Example: bench/chat-fanout/stable+canary-q8-seed42-run1
This must map to run metadata recorded with traces and captured loadgen logs.

Required telemetry to collect (per-run, per-variant):
- request_rps, token_rps (tokens/sec), avg_tokens_per_request
- latency_ms: p50, p95, p99 (end-to-end), and per-token latency where available
- GPU: utilization %, GPU memory used, active kernels/s, GPU stall reasons
- Host: CPU%, interrupts/ctx-switches, RSS, disk/io wait if local caching used
- Runtime: kv_cache_hits, kv_cache_misses, batch_size_distribution, queue_latency_ms
- Router: requests_sent_per_variant, fallback_count, retry_count
- Networking: egress_bps/ingress_bps, packet drops, NVLink throughput (if present)

Recommended phases and durations (practical defaults):
- Phase 0: Sanity check (2 min)
  - Verify route config, models loaded, health checks green. Small smoke load (1-2 rps).
- Phase 1: Micro-primer (5–10 min)
  - Send low-rate diverse prompts that touch model code paths and token lengths (1–5 rps each variant). Purpose: ensure code paths, quant kernels, and tokenizer caches compile/warm.
- Phase 2: Staggered coldfill (15–30 min total)
  - Sequentially ramp variants in the fanout in 2–5 minute offsets. Start stable variant first, then canary/quantized variant(s). This avoids immediate KV cross-pollination spikes and lets per-variant caches fill predictably.
- Phase 3: Steady ramp to target (15–30 min)
  - Linear or staircase ramp to the target request/tokens/s over 10–15 minutes. Hold at target for a minimum steady hold of 10 minutes.
- Phase 4: Steady hold and sampling (20–40 min)
  - Hold at target for 20–40 minutes and capture full telemetry. Split this time into three 5–10 minute windows for within-run variance checks.
- Phase 5: Cooldown (5 min)
  - Reduce load, capture graceful degradation behaviors and routing fallbacks.

Notes on staging the staggered coldfill:
- Order variants by expected startup cost and cache footprint: largest memory footprint first.
- If variants live on separate node pools, target primers to nodes directly (via routing hints) to avoid cross-node fan-in effects.
- If testing fallback policies, explicitly trigger a tiny proportion of failures to validate automatic fallbacks.

Load generator configuration (recommended fields and example):
- arrival_model: poisson | constant | fixed-burst (use poisson for production-like variability)
- concurrency: client-level concurrent connections (start conservative; 2x expected concurrency is good)
- rng_seed: integer (recorded) to enable deterministic sampling of prompts/sequence lengths
- prompt_mix: list of named templates with weights (short/medium/long, tool-calls, function-call variants)
- token_distribution: empirical histogram or percentiles (p10/p50/p90/p99 token lengths)
- inter_request_jitter_ms: 0–5 ms (tune down for low-jitter experiments)
- warmup_discard_window_sec: time at start of steady hold to ignore for metrics (recommended: 120s)

Example loadgen CLI snippet (template):
--arrival-model poisson --target-rps 600 --concurrency 48 --rng-seed 4231 --prompt-mix short:0.6,medium:0.3,long:0.1 --token-dist 12,32,64,128 --jitter-ms 2 --output run_metadata.json

Repeatability hygiene checklist (must be followed for benchmark-grade numbers):
- Use a recorded rng_seed and the same prompt mix file across runs.
- Evict any non-deterministic autoscaling policies or set them to fixed capacity for the entire experiment window.
- Pin model versions and confirm weights/quantization flags.
- Disable background jobs (backups, heavy infra jobs) on the test pool.
- Synchronize clocks (NTP) and record cluster time drift at start/end.
- Run at least 3 full independent runs (start-to-cooldown). Compare key metrics: tokens/s and p95 latency.
  - Acceptable run-to-run variation: coefficient of variation (CV) <= 3% for tokens/s and <= 5% for p95 latency. If not met, investigate priming sequence and noise sources.

Observability and post-run forensic queries (examples):
- Per-variant tail latency by minute (grouped by run window) to spot drift.
- Batch size distribution vs time to detect sudden batching changes.
- KV cache hit rate: look for step changes after primers.
- Router logs: verify per-request routing decisions (why a request chose variant X).
- GPU kernel latency histogram to diagnose kernel stalls.

Common pitfalls and mitigations:
- Pitfall: Primer too aggressive -> saturates NVLink causing other variants to underperform.
  - Mitigation: Use staggered primers and cap concurrency during primer phases.
- Pitfall: Autoscaler triggers scale-out mid-run -> invalidates steady-state measurement.
  - Mitigation: Freeze autoscaler or run on dedicated capacity.
- Pitfall: Shared OS-level caches (e.g., page cache) cause noise across experiments.
  - Mitigation: Reboot node between experiments when reproducibility needed or use isolated host pools.
- Pitfall: Unrecorded prompt changes / tokenization differences between runs.
  - Mitigation: Store canonical prompt files and tokenizer version in run metadata.

Regression detection and checklist to escalate:
1) If p95 latency increases by >10% at same tokens/s, capture a 15-minute trace and tag as "latency-regression".
2) If GPU occupancy decreases by >8% for same throughput, check kernel changes and scheduling preemption.
3) If batch-size distribution shifts toward smaller batches, inspect routing and queue-latency metrics.
4) Always attach the run_metadata.json and matching trace IDs to the bug report (link to GH or JIRA).

Run artifacts to store per experiment (required):
- run_metadata.json (loadgen flags, rng_seed, prompt file hash)
- compressed loadgen client logs (stdout/stderr)
- system telemetry snapshot (prometheus export, node metrics)
- router debug logs for the run window
- model server traces and kernel-level profiling output (if available)

Follow-ups and experiments to try if repeatability fails:
- Micro-benchmark each variant in isolation to build baseline occupancy curves.
- Run a collision matrix: primer-only vs target-only vs combined to estimate cross-pollination magnitude.
- Introduce controlled failure injection to validate fallback behavior and measure cost of fallback.
- Experiment with longer warmup windows for large quantized models (q4/q8) because JIT/compile costs can delay steady-state for tens of minutes.

Concluding notes (practical tips):
- When in doubt, lean on isolation: run single-variant baselines first then reintroduce fanout complexity.
- Always record the exact pipeline (router config, model flags, node ids) as part of the run metadata; replays are impossible without that.
- Traces beat heuristics: if the numbers look noisy, a 30-minute trace with sampler=100% for a 5 min window often reveals surprising contention (NVLink, scheduler preemption, kernel queueing).

Next steps (action items):
- (Aisha) Create a canonical prompt-mix repo and hash each mix; add as CI artifact for benchmark jobs.
- (Marco) Add a router debug endpoint to stream per-request routing decisions tagged with run_id.
- (Jordan) Draft a simple loadgen wrapper that enforces phase sequencing and writes run_metadata.json automatically.

Appendix: Minimal run metadata fields (JSON saved verbatim):
- run_id: string
- experiment_name: string
- target_rps: integer
- target_tokens_s: integer
- rng_seed: integer
- prompt_mix_hash: string
- variants_tested: comma-separated string
- node_pool_ids: comma-separated string
- autoscaler_state: frozen|enabled
- start_ts: iso8601
- end_ts: iso8601

(Keep this document short and actionable; expand into a wiki page if we want canonicalized templates and automated tooling.)
